title: Why Your Reps Are Guessing Who to Call
author: Xavier Singletary
summary: Most outbound fails before the first email. Not because the messaging is wrong, but because the rep has no idea which account to work, why that account matters, or who else is in the room. Here's what that's actually costing you, and how to fix it.
content:
Every morning, your reps sit down, open their CRM, and decide who to call. They scan a list of accounts. Maybe they sort by last-touched date. Maybe they pick the name they recognize. Maybe they go with whatever feels hot.

That's not prioritization. That's guessing.

And the cost of guessing isn't just a few wasted calls. It's pipeline that dies silently while your rep works an account that was never going to close.

What guessing actually costs you

Let's say you have five reps. Each one spends 30 minutes a day deciding what to work and digging up context on the account. That's two and a half hours a day, 12.5 hours a week, burned on research. At $80K loaded cost per rep, that's roughly $30,000 a year in selling time your team never gets back.

But the bigger cost isn't the time. It's the accounts that never get worked. The ones buried on page three of the CRM that matched your ICP perfectly but nobody noticed because there's no system surfacing them.

Why this happens in the first place

It's not your reps' fault. The tools give them lists. The tools don't tell them which list item to work, why, or what to say when they get there. Your CRM has accounts. Your enrichment tools have contacts. Gong has call recordings. Apollo has sequences. But none of them talk to each other.

Your reps are holding five tools in their head and trying to piece together a picture of each account manually. They spend more time researching than selling.

What the fix actually looks like

The fix isn't another tool. It's a system that connects the tools you already have and surfaces one clear answer every morning: work this account, for this reason, and here's what to say.

Here's what that system does:

  • Scores every account on Fit (how well they match your ICP) and Signal (what they're doing right now that indicates they might buy)
  • Assigns a verdict: STRIKE (work first), NURTURE (auto-enroll), QUALIFY (track), or KILL (drop)
  • Researches the highest-priority account, identifies the actual buying party, and writes a reasoned account plan
  • Stages the outreach in your rep's queue so all they do is review and send

The rep shows up, opens one thing, and goes. No guessing. No research. No "who do I call today."

A free win you can use tomorrow

You don't need to build the whole system to stop guessing. Here's something you can do in 20 minutes:

Pull your last 20 closed-won deals from your CRM. Find the three attributes that appear in 80% or more of them. Industry? Company size? Buyer persona? Write those three down. Now pull your open pipeline and score every account: 1 point for each of the three attributes that match. Rank by score. Work the top five first.

That's a manual Fit score. It's not automated, it's not real-time, and it doesn't account for signals. But it's better than guessing, and it takes 20 minutes.

If you want the automated version, the one that runs every morning without you touching it, that's what I build.
